Rashi on Eruvin 49a:1:1.hebrew: אף זו דברי ר' שמעון - אפילו להשתמש שתיהן עמה, ר' שמעון הוא דשרי; דהא אפילו אמצעית בשתיהן נמי שרי. אבל לרבנן, פליגי בכולה, ואמרו: שלשתן אסורין זו עם זו. ל"א: "אף זו דברי ר"ש" — ר' שמעון גופיה לא שרי אלא חיצונות באמצעית. וקשיא לי: הא תנן במתניתין "היא מותרת עמהן"? ועוד, מאי "אף"? הכי איבעי ליה למימר: "זו דברי ר"ש"! "אף" משמע דבתרוייהו שרי. ולשון אחרון זה שמעתי, וכן עיקר. "והיא מותרת עמהן" דמתניתין, מתרץ לך שמואל: דבהיתר שימוש שבאמצעית קאמר, דומיא ד"הוא מותר עמהן" דרישא; ואיידי דתנא רישא "הוא מותר עמהן", תני נמי סיפא. "ואף זו" — הכי משמע: אף ר' שמעון המיקל אוסר בזו, דאין אמצעית מותרת בחיצונות; אף איסור זה, ר"ש נמי אמרו כרבנן. ואלישנא קמא קשיא: מאי "ואזדא שמואל לטעמיה"? אי נמי הוה אמר כרב, הוה מצי נמי למימר לרבנן: עירבה עם שתיהן — אסורה עם שתיהן, דאין ב' רשויות משתמשות לרשות אחת:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:1:1.english: Even this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon - Even for both of them to use [the space] with it, it is Rabbi Shimon who permits [it], for according to him even the middle [courtyard using the space] in both of them is also permitted; but as for the Rabbis, they disagree with all of it, and said: All three of them are forbidden one with the other. Another interpretation: "Even this is the statement of Rabbi Shimon" — Rabbi Shimon himself permitted only the outer [courtyards to use the space] in the middle [courtyard]. And this poses a difficulty to me: But didn't we learn in the Mishnah, "it is permitted with them"? And furthermore, what is [the meaning of] "even"? It should have said, "This is the statement of Rabbi Shimon"; "even" implies that in both of them it is permitted. And this latter interpretation I heard [from my teachers], and so is the primary [explanation]. And [as for] "and it is permitted with them" in the Mishnah, Shmuel resolves [it] for you: that it refers to the permission of usage in the middle [courtyard], similar to "he is permitted with them" in the first clause; and since [the Mishnah] taught in the first clause "he is permitted with them," it also taught [parallel wording] in the latter clause. And "Even this" means as follows: Even Rabbi Shimon, who is lenient, prohibits in this case, for the middle [courtyard] is not permitted in the outer [courtyards]; even this prohibition, Rabbi Shimon also stated it, in agreement with the Rabbis. And according to the first interpretation, it is difficult: What is [the meaning of], "And Shmuel goes according to his reasoning"? Even if he had spoken in accordance with Rav, he could also have said according to the Rabbis: If it established an eiruv with both of them, it is forbidden with both of them, for two domains do not serve one domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:2:1.hebrew: תניא כוותיה דשמואל - דאפילו ר"ש לא התיר אמצעית בחיצונות, כדקתני: זו מביאה מתוך ביתה כו', ואילו אמצעית בחיצונות — לא קאמר:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:2:1.english: It was taught in accordance with Shmuel - For even Rabbi Shimon did not permit [carrying from] the middle [courtyard] into the outer [courtyards], as it teaches: "This [courtyard] brings from inside its house, etc.," whereas [carrying from] the middle [courtyard] into the outer [courtyards] — it does not state.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:2:2.english: To what is this comparable - It is referring to [the case of] three who rested on the road.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:2:3.hebrew: זו מביאה - באמצעית ואוכלת, וזו מביאה באמצעית ואוכלת:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:2:3.english: This [one] brings - Into the middle [courtyard] and eats [there], and that [one] brings into the middle [courtyard] and eats [there].

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:4:1.hebrew: ואזדא שמואל לטעמיה - דאמר: אף לר"ש, אין שתי רשויות משתמשות לרשות אחת:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:4:1.english: And Shmuel follows his line of reasoning - For he said: Even according to Rabbi Shimon, two domains do not make use of a single domain.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:4:2.english: A courtyard that is between two alleyways - [It is] open to both of them.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:4:3.hebrew: ה"ג עירבה עם שניהן אסורה עם שניהן - אפילו לרבי שמעון. והיינו שמואל לטעמיה, דאמר שמואל: הלכה כדברי המיקל בעירוב; ואי הוה שרי ר"ש בהא, לא הוה אמר שמואל: אסורה עם שניהן:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:4:3.english: This is the correct reading: If it established an eiruv with both of them, it is prohibited with both of them - Even according to Rabbi Shimon. And this is [the explanation of] "Shmuel follows his line of reasoning," as Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with the words of the one who is lenient regarding an eiruv. And if Rabbi Shimon permitted in this [case], Shmuel would not have said [that] it is prohibited with both of them.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:5:1.hebrew: לא עירבה עם שניהן - לא עירבה, לא עם זו ולא עם זו:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:5:1.english: [If] it did not establish an eiruv with both of them - It did not establish an eiruv, neither with this one nor with that one.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:5:2.hebrew: אוסרת על שניהן - מלהוציא מחצרותיהן למבוי. וכגון שרגילה כל ימות החול לצאת ולבא בשניהן דרך פתחים, דריסת הרגל שיש לה אוסרתן, כדמפרש. דאי לא הויא רגילה אלא בחד — לא אסרה אאידך. ואע"ג דרגילה עם שניהן, זו היא תקנתה: מערבת עם האחד, וגליא דעתה שנסתלקה מן האחר, ומותר האחד לעצמו:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:5:2.english: It prohibits both of them - From carrying out from their courtyards into the alleyway. And [this is] for example where it is accustomed on all weekdays to exit and enter through both of them by way of doorways; [for] the right of passage that it has prohibits them, as [the Gemara] explains. For if it were accustomed [to enter and exit] in only one, it would not prohibit the other. And even though it is accustomed with both of them, this is its remedy: it establishes an eiruv with the one, and [thereby] reveals its intention that it has removed itself from the other, and the one is permitted to itself.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:6:1.hebrew: היתה באחד רגילה - לצאת ולבא כל שעה, ובאחד אינה רגילה, ולא עירבה — לא עם זו ולא עם זו: זה שרגילה בו — אסור, שחצר זו אוסרת עליו, דמיניה הוא, והרי לא עירבה; והאחר — מותר, שאינה הימנו:
Rashi on Eruvin 49a:6:1.english: If it was accustomed to one - To go out and enter at all times, and to one it is not accustomed, and it did not make an eiruv — neither with this one nor with that one: That alleyway which it is accustomed to is forbidden, because this courtyard restricts it, as it belongs to it and behold, it did not make an eiruv; and the other alleyway is permitted, because it does not belong to it.

Rashi on Eruvin 49a:7:1.english: [The alleyway] it was accustomed to is permitted on its own - For [the courtyard] has removed itself from it.

Tosafot on Eruvin 49a:2:1.hebrew: זו מביאה מתוך ביתה ואוכלת לפ"ה דווקא נקט אבל אמצעית - בחיצונות לא. ולר"ת איכא למימר: דלרבותא נקט, דכ"ש אמצעית בחיצונות, דליכא למגזר כולי האי. ולפי' מהר"י נקט הא, משום דמהא פריך לרבנן: מאי שנא התם דפליגיתו וגזריתו, והכא לא גזריתו? מכדי "למה הדבר דומה" כו':
Tosafot on Eruvin 49a:2:1.english: "This one brings [food] from within her house and eats" - According to Rashi’s explanation, [the baraita] specifically taught [this], but the middle [courtyard bringing food] into the outer [courtyards] is not [permitted]. And according to Rabbeinu Tam, one can say that it taught [this] as a novelty, for all the more so [is it permitted for] the middle [courtyard to bring] into the outer [courtyards], as there is no [reason] to make such an extensive decree. And according to the explanation of Mahari, it taught this [case] because from this he poses a challenge to the Rabbis: What is the difference there that you dispute and make a decree, and here you do not make a decree? For after all, "to what is the matter comparable..."
